data.title: Currency Check | Rupee opens higher at 93.20 per dollar; Asian peers trade mixed
data.description:
The Indian rupee opened higher on November 20, as a surge in foreign inflows into Indian assets offsets the traditional pressure that a deterioration in sentiment exerts on emerging-market currencies.

The rupee opened with a gain of 9 paise at 93.20 per dollar, compared with previous close of 93.29.

According to Finrex, rupee to open at 93.29 levels after FPI bought Rs. 7411 crores of shares yesterday, the dollar amount of which will be sold in the markets today. The IPO was not subscribed well so the flows may not be good enough. Precious metals all fell big time yesterday with Gold touching $ 3560 per ounce down by 1.80% and silver touching $ 41.75 per ounce down by 6% which is more than 14-month low amid FED rate hike certainty and an ongoing rout in the AI trade on Wall Street which weighed on the yellow metal.

Exporters if they get the upside beyond 93.50 should sell for their exports with premiums higher while importers may now wait to buy near to 93.00 levels. Nothing much was taken from the US-RussiaChina summit held yesterday, it added.

Asian currencies traded on a mixed note against the US dollar, with most regional currencies registering losses. The Philippine peso was the worst performer, declining 0.31%, followed by the Taiwan dollar, which fell 0.27%. The Chinese renminbi weakened 0.18%, while the South Korean won and Indonesian rupiah slipped 0.15% and 0.12%, respectively. The Malaysian ringgit edged down 0.03%.

On the positive side, the Japanese yen gained 0.19%, emerging as the best-performing currency in the region, while the Thai baht and Singapore dollar edged higher by 0.06% and 0.04%, respectively.

The dollar is headed for a fourth straight weekly gain as demand tied to the Anthropic PBC IPO further lifts the currency that has been supported by expectations of further Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes and elevated US

Treasury yields.

data.title: Institutional Bitcoin ETF holdings clock record quarter after selling streak
data.description:
Institutional investment managers’ holdings of US Bitcoin exchange-traded funds climbed to a record high in the third quarter, as they reversed three straight quarters of net selling, according to regulatory filings.

The 13F filings, analyzed by Galaxy Research, show that the reporting companies added an equivalent of 49,229 Bitcoin (BTC) in the third quarter, outpacing the 47,054 Bitcoin they shed over the last three quarters combined. This lifted the reported total holdings to 356,491 BTC, the highest on record.

“The quarter’s accumulation was the work of a few dozen large institutions,” wrote Galaxy’s head of firmwide research Alex Thorn.

Quarterly 13F filings provide a point-in-time snapshot of US-listed securities held by reporting institutional investment managers. Thorn said half of the net addition of spot Bitcoin ETF shares came from advisors and wealth platforms.

Wells Fargo posted the largest increase, adding the equivalent of 14,636 Bitcoin, making it the largest institutional holder of spot Bitcoin ETPs. Other strong gainers included Brevan Howard, Bank of America, Millennium Management and Jane Street.

Largest holders of spot Bitcoin ETP positions in Q3. Source: Galaxy Research

“Early readings suggest longer-term holders make up a growing share of the spot Bitcoin ETF investor base,” Bitwise analyst Camran Khosravi previously told Cointelegraph, when the first batch of 13F filings had begun to come in.

The number of managers reporting a position in a spot Bitcoin ETF also rose for the first time in three quarters, increasing by 191 to 2,166.

This all came as Bitcoin gained about 43% in the third quarter, ending September at $83,621.

Meanwhile, Galaxy’s data shows BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust accounted for the largest share of holdings reported by 13F filers, with the equivalent of 232,453 BTC held by the filers. This was followed by the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund.

Together, the two funds were responsible for 77% of all Bitcoin held by the reporting entities.

Bitcoin equivalent held by 13F filers. Source: Galaxy Research

US Bitcoin ETFs post two months of outflows

The record institutional holdings in Q3 contrast with more recent weakness in US spot Bitcoin ETFs, with net monthly outflows reaching $515 million in October and $2.9 billion of outflows month to date, according to TFTC’s Bitcoin ETF tracker.

Earlier in the month, Bitwise head of research André Dragosch told Cointelegraph he viewed the selling as “related to a short-term risk-off environment rather than a structural change in institutional sentiment.”

data.title: China's fuel oil exports for bunkering ease in October while imports rebound
data.description:
China's fuel oil exports, mainly for marine fuel bunkering, fell in October after a strong September, while fuel oil imports rebounded, customs data showed on Friday.

October export volumes totalled 1.62 million metric tons, or about 333,000 barrels a day, down 37% from September but up 32% from the same month a year ago, according to General Administration of Customs data.

Bunker export activity slowed in October with more vessels calling at regional Asian hub Singapore, which offered lower prices during most of October for the mainstay low-sulphur fuel grade than Zhoushan and Shanghai ports, market sources said.

Meanwhile, fuel oil imports into China, which typically head to refineries and the marine fuel blending pool, recovered to a seven-month high in October as feedstock demand improved.

Customs data showed imports totaled 1.95 million tons for October, up 72% from September and 4% higher than a year earlier.

data.title: Kuwait offers second gasoline cargo this month in FOB tender, document shows
data.description:
By Mohi Narayan

Kuwait Petroleum Corp has offered 34,000-35,000 metric tons of 93-octane non-oxygenated gasoline in a tender on a free-on-board (FOB) basis from its Mina Al-Ahmadi port, a document reviewed by Reuters showed on Friday.

The cargo is scheduled to load between December 9 and December 10, according to the tender, which closed on Wednesday.

The state-run refiner sold the same grade fuel for late-November loading at a premium of around $180 to $200 per ton to Middle East naphtha quotes, market participants said.

It was KPC's first gasoline offer via a tender after a gap of several months since the war in the Gulf broke out.

Oil companies typically do not comment on tenders.

data.title: CGI and Learning Links Foundation launch Centre of Excellence for AI & Innovation at MEI Polytechnic College
data.description:
Initiative to provide hands-on learning opportunities in AI and emerging technologies for more than 1,250 students

BENGALURU, India, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CGI (TSX: GIB.A) (), one of the largest independent IT and business consulting services firms in the world, has inaugurated the CGI Centre of Excellence for AI & Innovation at MEI Polytechnic College in Bengaluru, in collaboration with Learning Links Foundation (LLF). Designed, funded and strategically planned by CGI, the centre creates a dedicated space where students can learn, experiment, and develop practical solutions using emerging technologies.

The centre will provide hands-on learning opportunities to more than 1,250 students in artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), robotics, 3D design and printing, electronics and digital fabrication. Students will participate in project-based learning, technical challenges and innovation activities that help connect classroom concepts with practical applications. Equipped with development boards, sensors, embedded systems, robotic platforms, and comprehensive prototyping tools, the facility empowers students to build, test, and refine solutions to real-world problems.

"Access to technology can open new paths for students when it is paired with the opportunity to experiment, build and solve real problems," said Deepak Shenoy, Senior Vice-President and Business Unit Leader, Asia Pacific Global Delivery Center of Excellence, CGI. "Through this centre, we want students to engage with AI and emerging technologies in a practical and responsible way, and to build the confidence and skills to turn their ideas into solutions. This initiative reflects CGI's commitment to supporting the communities where we live and work by creating more equitable opportunities for the future."

"The CGI Centre of Excellence for AI & Innovation will give our students the opportunity to experience emerging technologies in a practical and engaging environment," said L. N. Reddy, Principal, MEI Polytechnic College. "It will complement their technical education by allowing them to experiment, build prototypes and develop solutions, while strengthening the confidence and problem-solving skills they will need in a rapidly changing technology landscape."

"The journey from classroom learning to real-world innovation begins with access to the right opportunities," said Sudha Priyadarshan, Senior Vice President, Learning Links Foundation. "Through this collaboration with CGI and MEI Polytechnic College, students will be able to explore AI, IoT, robotics and 3D printing through structured, hands-on learning. We look forward to supporting them as they develop future-ready skills and learn how to transform their ideas into working solutions."

About CGI

Founded in 1976, CGI is among the largest independent IT and business consulting services firms in the world. With 94,000 consultants and professionals across the globe, CGI delivers an end-to-end portfolio of capabilities, from strategic IT and business consulting to systems integration, managed IT and business process services and intellectual property solutions. CGI works with clients through a local relationship model complemented by a global delivery network that helps clients digitally transform their organizations and accelerate results. CGI Fiscal 2026 reported revenue is CA$16.57 billion and CGI shares are listed on the TSX (GIB.A) and the NYSE (GIB). Learn more at cgi.com.

data.title: PTT Likely Resilient Play in Normalizing Energy-Price Environment — Market Talk
data.description: PTT is likely a resilient play in a normalizing energy-price environment, TTB Wealth Securities' Yupapan Polpornprasert says in a note. Its integrated business model, including stable gas and pipeline operations, provides a more defensive earnings profile than its subsidiaries, the analyst says. Together with stable earnings from subsidiary PTT Exploration & Production's gas sales and steady contributions from oil retail, these businesses account for around 53% of PTT's profit, giving meaningful buffer against cyclical weakness. The energy conglomerate is expected to deliver attractive dividend yields of 8.6% in 2026 and 6.1% in 2027. The brokerage raises the stock's target price to 46.00 baht from 43.00 baht, with an unchanged buy rating. Shares are 0.5% higher at 37.60 baht. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

data.title: Iron ore rises on restocking hopes, but set for weekly loss
data.description:
By Emily Ou Yong

Iron ore futures rose on Friday on hopes of year-end restocking by steel mills, though the contracts remained set for a weekly loss after breaking through previous lows earlier in the week amid weak demand and high port stocks.

The most-traded January iron ore contract on China's Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE) traded 1.08% higher at 655.5 yuan ($98.33) a metric ton, as of 0300 GMT.

The contract has lost 2.24% so far this week.

The benchmark December iron ore <SZZFZ6> on the Singapore Exchange was 0.62% higher at $88.95 a ton, losing 1.66% so far this week.

Steel mills' raw material costs have fallen with iron ore prices, and year-end restocking could provide some short-term support, though low profits mean purchases are likely to be cautious, analysts from broker Minmetals Futures said in a note.

Imported sintering powder inventories at 114 steel mills rose 1.29 million tons to 27.75 million tons this week, data from consultancy Mysteel showed.

Iron ore inventory at major Chinese ports rose 0.74% from the previous week to 157.36 million tons, data from consultancy Steelhome showed.

Futures broke through previous lows on November 16 and fell as low as 638.5 yuan a ton on November 18, as expectations of tighter US Federal Reserve policy sapped risk appetite, the Minmetals analysts said.

Elsewhere, executives at iron ore majors BHP and Rio Tinto are due to meet with China's premier and business leaders in Beijing on Friday, amid increasingly fraught negotiations between Australia's top miners and China's state iron ore buyer, China Mineral Resources Group.

Other steelmaking ingredients on the DCE climbed, with coking coal NYMEX:ACT1! and coke (DCJcv1) up 3.34% and 3.67%, respectively.

Steel benchmarks on the Shanghai Futures Exchange were mixed. Rebar rose 0.94% and hot-rolled coil gained 0.61%, while stainless steel fell 0.94%.

($1 = 6.6665 Chinese yuan)

data.title: Japan Core CPI Likely to Accelerate to 2.7% in November — Market Talk
data.description: Japan's November core consumer prices, which exclude fresh food, are expected to rise by around 2.7% from a year earlier, while the core-core measure, which strips out both fresh food and energy, is projected to increase around 2.3%, according to Okasan Securities estimates. Both indexes were up 2.2% in October, Friday's data showed. Price increases for items affected by Middle East tensions and artificial-intelligence demand stayed mild in the October report, though wholesale price data for the month shows supply-chain cost pressures are picking up again and will likely feed into retail prices going forward, the brokerage's economists say. (megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com)

data.title: Artificial Intelligence Boom Likely Becoming Unsustainable — Market Talk
data.description: The artificial intelligence boom is likely becoming increasingly unsustainable, Capital Economics says in a note. Earnings expectations have been stretched, the firm's economists say. High valuations and huge investment plans are based on assumptions about AI's future profitability that may prove too optimistic, they add. As investors become more skeptical about future returns, Capital Economics expects a significant correction in technology stocks followed by a slowdown in U.S. AI investment. The research firm expects the U.S. stock market to fall around 30% from peak to trough by end-2027. The economists also except a similar peak-to-trough drop in Taiwan and a 50% selloff in South Korea. (amanda.lee@wsj.com)

data.title: Vedanta share price target cut by its biggest bear - Here's are the concerns highlighted
data.description:
Vedanta Ltd.'s share price target has been cut by global investment banking firm Citi, in its latest note on Friday, November 20.

Citi has maintained its "sell" rating on the Vedanta, the Anil Agarwal-owned mining conglomerate, and has cut its price target to ₹210 from ₹235 earlier. This is the lowest price target on the street for the stock.

In fact, Citi is the only firm among the 12 analysts who track Vedanta Ltd., that has a "sell" rating on the stock.

Citi wrote in its note that its commodities team sees the physical zinc market as "relatively balanced" in 2027, with risks skewing towards moderation of elevated positioning in 2027.

Tepid long-term structural demand exposure for zinc, risks that mine supply ease, and LME premium over the Shanghai Futures Exchange eases are some of the key risks for Zinc positioning moderating next year.

As per Citi's analysts Zinc prices in CY2028 are seen at $3,700, compared to the current spot price of $3,550. With silver being 40% of attributable Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation and Amortisation (EBITDA) of the company, its upsides would be predicated on macro economic factors easing, Citi wrote in its note.

For 2028, Citi has incorporated Silver prices to be at $60 an ounce, compared to the current spot price, which has correct to nearly $40 an ounce level.

Citi wrote further that every $100 per tonne move in Zinc-Lead prices on the LME, will impact Vedanta's EBITDA by 4%, and its fair value per share by ₹12. Every $10 an ounce change in Silver impacts Vedanta's EBITDA by 7% and its fair value by ₹16 per share.

Another concern highlighted by Citi for Vedanta is surrounding its use of cash, as the company is no longer bound by its old dividend policy after the demerger of its various entities in June this year.

Hindustan Zinc's volume growth is likely only in the second half of financial year 2029, although Zinc International should benefit from Gamsberg Phase 2.

Among the 12 analysts tracking Vedanta, nine of them have a "buy" rating, two have a "hold" rating.

Shares of Vedanta ended 0.7% lower on Thursday at ₹243.7. The stock is up only 3% so far in the last one month.

data.title: Interest rate cuts are coming: Latest expert views on when and how much
data.description:
Key points:
  • The RBA has hiked interest rates five times this year, taking the cash rate to 4.85% as it battles stubborn inflation, while household budgets have been squeezed and property prices have fallen sharply.
  • October's jobs data showed 43,500 jobs lost and sending unemployment to 4.9% – marking the largest two-month decline in employment since 2000, excluding COVID.
  • We bring you the latest reactions from three major investment banks, what the market says about the timing of the first rate cut, and where opportunities may exist for ASX investors.

It's been a brutal year for Australian borrowers. The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) has raised the cash rate five times in 2026, taking it to 4.85%, in a bid to bring inflation back under control. Mortgage holders are feeling the squeeze, and property prices have plunged.

Then came yesterday's October Labour Force report. Seasonally adjusted employment fell by 43,500, following September's 36,400 decline, and the unemployment rate jumped to 4.9% – the highest since October 2021.

The experts' views on the economy and the future path of the official cash rate that’s so important to its success or failure – have changed overnight. Below, I bring you the latest from three of the major investment banks and, most importantly, when the market believes the first round of interest rate relief will arrive.

Expert takes: Is the Australian economy stuffed?

UBS called the October jobs report another disappointment, noting the fall came in well below its own forecast of a 15,000 increase and the market's expectation of 20,000 jobs added. Annual employment growth slowed to just 0.6%, the weakest since 2021, and the three-month average fell to a loss of 17,000 jobs a month. UBS now expects unemployment to rise to 5.25% in coming quarters.

Macquarie notes the 80,000 jobs lost over the past two months is the largest two-month fall since 2000, excluding COVID, with 112,000 part-time roles lost against a 32,000 rise in full-time jobs. It points out that the rise in unemployment has been driven by workers aged 25 and over, a less volatile group than younger workers, suggesting labour demand is genuinely weakening. Macquarie also notes that some of the fall may reflect volatility in the survey sample.

Morgan Stanley described the result as 'material weakness', noting unemployment is already where the RBA expected it to be at the end of next year. The bank forecasts unemployment will climb to 5.4%, and says the data adds to the RBA Board's concerns about slowing activity, while stronger wages growth still points to persistent cost pressures.

Note none of the three banks is forecasting a recession yet – indeed UBS's strategists say explicitly they don't expect one. Let’s hope they’re right!

Interest rate relief is on the way

UBS has brought forward its forecast for the first rate cut to August 2027, from November 2027, and no longer expects any further hikes. It now sees a 75 basis point easing cycle (up from its previous forecast for 50 basis points), with cuts in November 2027 and February 2028, which would take the cash rate to 4.10%.

Morgan Stanley expects an extended hold from here, before cuts in August and November 2027 that would take the cash rate to 4.35% by the end of next year.

Macquarie says the data strengthens the view that the RBA's tightening cycle is finished, and that a continuation of the recent labour market weakness could see the RBA begin to reverse some of its rate as soon as mid-2027.

ASX 30 Day Interbank Cash Rate Futures implied yield curve

Takeaways from the Cash Rate Futures implied yield curve chart:

  • Six weeks ago the market expected rates to keep rising. On 1 October, with the cash rate at 4.60%, futures priced a peak of about 4.96% by mid-2027. That’s more than one further hike on top of the one the RBA delivered in November. The curve was still 4.89% by March 2028, so no cuts were priced at all.

  • By the eve of the jobs data the hike bets had mostly faded. On 18 November the curve peaked at just 4.905% in March–April 2027, only slightly above today’s 4.85% cash rate. A single cut was priced by April 2028, when the curve fell to 4.59%.

  • The October jobs report wiped out the last of the hike risk overnight. On 19 November the curve fell below the current cash rate from February 2027 onwards. Contracts from mid-2027 dropped 15–22 basis points in one session. A first cut is now fully priced by October 2027, with August 2027 at 4.64%, about an 85% chance. A second cut is almost fully priced by April 2028, at 4.365%.

Where should ASX investors be looking to buy the dip?

UBS's equity strategists believe peak rates are now behind us, making a 'rate pivot' trade into domestic consumer and housing cyclicals look tempting. But they caution it's still too early, with the risk of earnings downgrades building. Recent trading updates show sales growth running flat on the previous corresponding period, down from 1.1% in August and 3.4% in February – and with inflation running at around 4%, that means volumes are going backwards.

S&P-ASX 200 Real Estate Sector Index (XJR) intraday chart

UBS's preferred starting point is Real Estate, which it upgraded to neutral in early October. The sector has historically been first to move and has the highest sensitivity to a rate pivot, and UBS says it remains as cheap relative to the market as it has been outside the GFC. It prefers names without housing exposure.

Consumer Discretionary has historically had the second-highest sensitivity to a rate pivot, but UBS remains underweight, arguing valuations aren't yet cheap and earnings risks are building. It's also underweight the Banks, citing stretched valuations and growing tail risks to earnings as unemployment rises.

Is there really 'always' a silver lining?

The economy is bad, and that's typically not good for stocks. But the stock market looks forward, not backward, and investors will start trying to price the risk of the economy getting worse against the timing of it eventually getting better.

Next week's October CPI print on 25 November and the RBA's 8 December decision will shape that calculation, followed by November's jobs data on 17 December. As always, the trend is your friend, so watch closely the performance of the most interest rate sensitive sectors like real estate, consumer discretionary and the big banks.

References: This article draws on the ABS Labour Force, Australia, October 2026 release (19 November 2026); and broker research from UBS (Australian Economic Comment and Australian Equity Strategy, 19 November 2026), Macquarie (Australian Labour Market: Could we see a policy reversal?, 19 November 2026) and Morgan Stanley (Australia Macro+: October Labour Force – Material Weakness, 19 November 2026).

data.title: Indonesia current account gap narrows significantly in Q3
data.description:
Indonesia's current account deficit narrowed significantly to 0.5% of gross domestic product in the third quarter, compared with a revised deficit of 3.4% of GDP in the previous three months, central bank data showed on Friday.

Its balance of payments recorded a surplus of $80 million in the third quarter, a swing from the $882 million deficit in the second quarter.

data.title: Malaysia's Inflation, Interest Rates Might Rise in 2027 — Market Talk
data.description: Malaysia's inflation could edge higher to 2.3% in 2027 from an expected 1.9% in 2026, as elevated input and operating costs gradually pass through to consumer prices, Affin Hwang IB analysts Farah Hanini and Vincent Loo say in a note. While targeted subsidies and electricity bill protections will likely continue to contain price pressures this year, inflation is expected to become more persistent, they say. Bank Negara Malaysia is expected to raise the policy rate by 25 bps in 2027, following a pause in 2026, amid firmer domestic demand and broader inflationary pressures, they add. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)

data.title: India's Stylam Industries buys 51% stake in paper maker
data.description:
Indian laminates manufacturer Stylam Industries (BSE: 526951) will acquire 51% of Haripur Kraft Co., a paper producer in Himachal Pradesh, for a capital contribution of up to INR224.4mn ($2.40mn), the company said in a stock exchange filing on November 19, 2026.

Stylam’s board approved the deal earlier that day at a meeting lasting half an hour. The purchase gives Stylam a stake in a supplier of kraft paper, a primary raw material for its laminates. The Chandigarh-based company called the move backward integration. It said owning part of the producer would protect it from price swings and supply disruptions, give it tighter control over quality and improve its competitive position over the long term. Haripur Kraft is a partnership firm formed on October 1, 2011.

It makes semi kraft paper and paper products at a plant in Solan district with a daily capacity of 125 tonnes. Stylam will pay in cash, putting capital into the firm in one or more stages under the terms of the partnership deed. The contribution was set on the basis of a valuation agreed with the current partners. Stylam and the existing partners will control the firm jointly after the transaction. The partners will each retain 24.5%.

Stylam said the partners are not related parties and that none of its promoters, promoter group members or group companies has any interest in the firm. The deal does not need any government or regulatory approval. Stylam expects to close it on or before January 31, 2027, provided the conditions set out in the deed are met.

data.title: FISV Stock Slumps Most In 5 Months: Portfolio Review Fuels Speculation, But Analyst Casts Doubt On Debit Network Sale
data.description:
Key points:
  • The analyst said that recent commentary from Fiserv around portfolio optimization has reignited speculation that the company could monetize some non-core assets, particularly its debit networks.
  • The firm has an ‘Outperform’ rating on the shares with a $70 price target.
  • Chief Executive Officer Takis Georgakopoulos said in the latest earnings call that Fiserv will review its businesses, products and capital commitments, which will extend beyond lower-growth businesses.

Shares of Fiserv, Inc. (FISV) slumped to their lowest level since June, losing more than 6% at close. However, the stock recovered marginally overnight, turning green in extended trading hours.

According to The Fly, Keefe Bruyette said that based on management’s recent commentary, the sale of its debit networks seems unlikely.

Keefe Bruyette’s Stance On Fiserv 

The analyst said that recent commentary from Fiserv around portfolio optimization has reignited speculation that the company could monetize some non-core assets, particularly its debit networks. While the strategic rationale is understandable, a debit network sale is unlikely given regulatory considerations and a limited buyer universe, it said in a research note.

However, Keefe said that it believes Fiserv has other slower growth businesses representing 10% of total revenue that could be candidates for monetization, potentially providing capital for buybacks while improving margins. The firm has an ‘Outperform’ rating on the shares with a $70 price target.

FISV’s Debit Network Sale 

Earlier this year, the Wall Street Journal reported that major banks including Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase, PNC Financial Services Group and Wells Fargo had held preliminary talks with Fiserv about a debit network sale.

Chief Executive Officer Takis Georgakopoulos recently said that Fiserv is migrating clients to one of its two debit networks and will sell the other if it receives a suitable offer. The alternative would be to wind down one network.

That migration will conclude “over the next few quarters,” he said at the Citi 15th annual fintech conference. Fiserv owns the Star and Accel debit networks.

In the latest earnings call, Georgakopoulos said the company will review its businesses, products, and capital commitments, extending beyond lower-growth businesses. This will help assess whether individual products are best-in-class and whether Fiserv has the ability to compete effectively in each area.

He added that the company would consider alternatives for products where it does not see a clear path to compete, while seeking to avoid disruption to clients.

FISV Retail Stance

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around FISV stock was ‘bearish’ at the time of writing, while message volumes jumped over 133% in 24 hours, as per platform data.

One user said, “$FISV this very well could be in the 30s by next quarter. I mean look at $FIS trading at 3x PE.” FISV stock last closed at $56.62.

Another user said, “$FISV It seems that a new downward spiral has started. I hate it when you have an indifferent board that doesn’t care about the share price… short sellers are having fun with this one.”

FISV stock is down more than 15% year-to-date.

data.title: Gold set for worst week in eight months as firm dollar, Fed hike bets weigh
data.description:
Key points:
  • Gold eyes biggest weekly fall since March
  • Silver, platinum and palladium head for weekly declines
  • Fed's Paulson says Fed will need to raise rates again
  • US dollar holds near 19-month high

By Sukanya Mitra

Gold prices slipped on Friday and were headed for their worst week in eight months, as a resilient US dollar and expectations of a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike in December weighed on bullion.

Spot gold fell 1.9% to $3,551.68 per ounce by 0257 GMT, after hitting its lowest level since September 2025 earlier in the session. Bullion was down about 8.9% this week, its sharpest weekly decline since the week of March 20. US gold futures for December delivery slid 3.6% to $3,551.90.

"There seems to be a bit of forced liquidation going on across the market in general, with expectations of imminent US rate hikes and inflation that could be persistent, leading to high yields and a higher US dollar as a result, pressuring gold," said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com.

Asian shares slid on Friday, putting them on track for their worst week since 2020, as Anthropic's debut failed to restore investor faith in the AI sector.

The dollar held near a 19-month high on Friday, extending its recent rally and making greenback-priced bullion more expensive for holders of other currencies.

Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday the Fed will need to raise interest rates again because inflation is too high, while arguing that shared understanding matters more than explicit guidance on the rate outlook.

Markets see a 97.3% chance of a 25-basis-point US rate hike in December, while the probability of a larger 50-basis-point move is priced at 2.7%, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, reducing its appeal to investors.

Elsewhere, Swiss gold exports fell to 109.7 metric tons in October, down 34% from the prior month as deliveries to Britain were lower, Swiss customs data showed on Thursday.

Among other metals, spot silver fell 2% to $41.9 per ounce, platinum dropped 2% to $1,317.00, and palladium slid 2.3% to $888.66. All three metals were headed for weekly losses.

data.title: Yesway Announces Pricing of Secondary Public Offering
data.description:
FORT WORTH, Texas, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Yesway, Inc. (“Yesway”) today announced the pricing of the underwritten secondary offering of 5,000,000 shares of Yesway’s Class A common stock by certain of its existing stockholders at a price to the public of $19.00 per share. In addition, the underwriters of the offering have a 30-day option to purchase from the selling stockholders up to 750,000 additional shares of Class A common stock at the public offering price, less underwriting discounts and commissions. The selling stockholders will receive all of the net proceeds from this offering. The offering is expected to close on November 23, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.

Morgan Stanley is acting as lead bookrunning manager for the offering. J.P. Morgan and Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC are acting as active bookrunning managers. Barclays, BMO Capital Markets, KeyBanc Capital Markets, Guggenheim Securities, Raymond James, and William Blair are also acting as bookrunners.

A registration statement relating to this offering was declared effective by the Securities and Exchange Commission on November 19, 2026. The offering is made only by means of a prospectus. About Yesway

Established in 2015 and headquartered in Fort Worth, Texas, Yesway is an award-winning convenience store operator with approximately 420 stores across eight states in the Midwest and Southwest. data.title: US Senate passes bipartisan bill to speed energy, infrastructure projects
data.description:
The US Senate voted 62-33 on Thursday to pass a sweeping bipartisan energy permitting bill to speed approvals for large projects such as power plants, transmission lines, mines and data centers, marking Congress' most significant effort in years to ease bottlenecks blamed for rising energy costs.

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act now heads to the Republican-controlled House of Representatives. If it passes, President Donald Trump has said he will sign the bill into law.

data.title: Asian shares head for worst week since 2020 as AI rout deepens
data.description:
Key points:
  • Asia stocks on track for worst week since Covid hit
  • Anthropic's historic debut fails to revive faith in AI trade
  • Dollar holds near 19-month peak on safe-haven flows

By Jiaxing Li and Rae Wee

Asian shares fell on Friday, heading for their worst week since 2020, as Anthropic's debut failed to restore investor faith in the AI sector, while the dollar extended a rally on safe-haven flows.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan <.MISX00000PUS> lost 3.2%, its biggest single-day drop in over a month. The gauge has now sunk 8.3% this week, its worst performance since March 2020.

Japan's Nikkei tumbled 4.1% and was headed for a 6.8% weekly drop, while South Korea's KOSPI fell 4.4% and was set to end the week 7.1% lower. Taiwan shares <.TWII> were down 5% on Friday and 16% for the week, their biggest weekly decline since 1991.

The moves in Asia followed losses of more than 2% for the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX and the Nasdaq Composite after Anthropic, the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company, saw its shares surge in a historic debut but the euphoria failed to lift other stocks.

"Risk aversion intensified as investors continued to unwind crowded positioning and reassess the broader macro backdrop following Anthropic's record-shattering IPO," said Preston Pagli, markets analyst at Citi.

He added that Nvidia's blowout earnings earlier in the week failed to become the reset markets had hoped for, while sentiment deteriorated further after Anthropic's IPO failed to spark a broader rally.

Further adding to the unease, a report on AMD from a media outlet associated with short-selling fund Hunterbrook Capital raised concerns that the chipmaker's ties to Chinese entities, some linked to blacklisted firms, could draw greater US regulatory scrutiny to the sector.

The AI trade has already been battered by Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia , growing momentum for the anti-data-centre movement following Democrats' sweep of the US midterm elections, and concerns over the sector's rising debt loads.

"No one headline drove the roll though some pointed to an AMD short report which tapered overall sentiment. Overall, it just felt like more questions than answers out there today with most wondering what gets this tape to feel better?" said Goldman Sachs analysts in a trading note.

They said asset managers and hedge funds net-sold macro products while they net-bought pockets of consumer and financials, with liquidity remaining poor, which is exacerbating price action.

US stock futures also pointed to further losses, with the S&P 500 futures down 0.2% and Nasdaq futures down 0.6% in Asia on Friday.

DOLLAR EXTENDS RALLY, TREASURY YIELDS DIP ON RISK AVERSION

As risk sentiment took a beating, the US dollar extended its rally on safe-haven bids, while also being supported by growing expectations of a more hawkish Federal Reserve.

Fed funds futures imply that a quarter-point rate hike next month is essentially locked in, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

The dollar index last traded steady at 103.86, after rising to its highest since April 2025 this week, and is now on track to post its fourth week of gains.

In government debt, US Treasury yields eased as the sharp equity selloff pushed investors toward safe-haven bonds. The yield on benchmark 10-year Treasury notes held steady at 5.02%, near a one-week low. The 2-year yield (US2YT=RR) touched 4.749%, compared with a US close of 4.779%.

Oil prices were mostly steady after an earlier spike, as reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz offset pressure from rising US crude inventories and forecasts for a global oil surplus. (O/R)

Brent crude futures rose 0.4% to $92.37 a barrel but remained on track for a third week of declines.

Non-interest-bearing gold slid 2.5% to $3,533.40 an ounce and was headed for a 9% weekly loss.
